decisions.decision: cmd/ci-plan/main.go gains --task-id and --correlation-id flags; an empty or whitespace value falls back to built-in defaults task_id=V2-000 and correlation_id=local-component-evidence; the resolved task id is checked against ^V2-[0-9]{3}$ and the process fails before writing any record. Makefile forwards the make variables EVIDENCE_TASK_ID and EVIDENCE_CORRELATION_ID into those flags from the component, evidence-all targets. No environment variable is read.
decisions.rationale: argv is the only reliable injection channel through the common entrypoint because devbox run --pure strips inherited environment variables, while make VAR=value survives on argv. Empty-means-default keeps scripts/affected.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml (make affected / make candidate-affected) working unchanged, so backward compatibility is preserved without touching CI. Replacing the hardcoded V2-005 removes the false attribution of local evidence to an unrelated active task, which is the defect class that failed V2-024; V2-000 is the terminal bootstrap identity and the schema pattern ^V2-[0-9]{3}$ forbids a non-task sentinel string. Fail-fast pattern validation prevents ci-plan from ever writing evidence that violates contracts/schemas/evidence.json.

decisions.decision: Add --all (select every manifest component regardless of --changed) and --keys (populate the already declared but unused Plan.EvidenceKeys for the selected components) to cmd/ci-plan, plus Makefile targets evidence-all and evidence-keys.
decisions.rationale: Generating all 23 records today requires the side effect of naming an all_on_change path (for example --changed Makefile), which records a false changed set in the plan output and in every generated record. An explicit --all states the intent. --keys makes the component keys observable so the aggregate attestation can be recomputed and machine-verified later; the JSON field is evidence_keys with omitempty, so existing callers see byte-identical output when --keys is absent.

decisions.decision: internal/ci/planner.go and internal/ci/planner_test.go are not modified. Both new flags are implemented in package main using the exported ci.EvidenceKeyWithManifest and the manifest component list.
decisions.rationale: Evidence key semantics are the invariant this task depends on; changing them would invalidate every key and require re-interpreting validation.md sections 8 and 11 (product/invariant scope, which escalates to product_orchestrator). Keeping the planner untouched means TestAffectedReverseClosure, TestManifestRejectsCycle, TestTrackedOwnership and TestCandidateComponentsDoesNotRequireUnchangedEvidence cannot regress.

decisions.decision: build/evidence/<component>-<key>.json stays ephemeral, gitignored (/build/ in .gitignore) developer feedback consumed only by ci.CandidateComponents; it is never copied into .agents and never committed. Exactly one record is committed: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-008-candidate-aggregate.json plus its .agents/v2/evidence/index.json entry.
decisions.rationale: Committing 23 per-component records would put content-addressed, per-tree data into the ledger, so every later commit would invalidate and require rewriting all of them, and the index bijection would churn on every change. One aggregate attestation records the closure fact (23/23 fresh keys at a named commit) while the per-component records remain reproducible from source by make evidence-all. This also keeps the default V2-000 identity of local records out of the canonical ledger.

decisions.decision: The committed record is evidence-v1 with id ev-v2-008-candidate-aggregate, task_id V2-008, correlation_id v2-008-candidate-gate, component candidate-aggregate, result passed, and evidence_key = sha256 over the concatenation, for all components sorted by id, of component_id + LF + evidence_key + LF (64 hex, satisfies ^[a-f0-9]{16,128}$). checks contains one entry per component (name = component id, argv = the component's real entrypoint invocation, summary = 'component=<id> evidence_key=<64hex> base_commit=<sha>') followed by entries for evidence-all, candidate, evidence-keys and check. The index entry carries evidence_hash = sha256 of the final attestation file bytes.
decisions.rationale: contracts/schemas/evidence.json is additionalProperties:false, so the 23 (component, key) pairs can only be carried inside checks[].summary; that keeps the per-component keys machine-parseable without a schema change (a schema change would cross the contracts boundary and require product_orchestrator escalation). The aggregate digest is derived only from data present in the record, so a verifier can recompute it from the summaries and compare against evidence_key. evidence_hash must be sha256(file bytes) because internal/contracts TestActiveEvidenceIndex compares it with sha256.Sum256 of the raw artifact.

decisions.decision: Two commits. Commit A carries the code, test, Makefile and docs change (and the V2-008 packets). With the tree at commit A staged and clean, make evidence-all then make candidate produce and verify the 23 keys; those keys and commit A's sha (base_commit) are what the attestation records. Commit B contains only .agents/v2/evidence/V2-008-candidate-aggregate.json and .agents/v2/evidence/index.json; after staging it, make component COMPONENT=task-ledger re-mints exactly the one invalidated record and make candidate must be green again on commit B's tree. Later verification of the attestation is: check out base_commit in a scratch worktree, run make evidence-keys, and require the printed map to equal the pairs in checks[].summary and their fold to equal evidence_key. Verifying the current tree is always make candidate, never the attestation.
decisions.rationale: No single self-consistent commit exists: the task-ledger key preimage includes the attestation file, so the file would have to contain a hash of its own bytes. The blast radius of committing it is provably one component: task-ledger owns .agents/** , has no public_contracts, and no component declares it as a dependency, so no other key moves. Measured in this repository: keys are computed from git ls-files (the index) plus working-tree content, so an untracked attestation leaves make candidate green ({"candidate":true}) and staging the same file makes exactly task-ledger fail with 'missing evidence for task-ledger key ...'; re-minting one record costs make component-contracts (seconds). Attesting a named parent commit is also what validation.md section 8 asks for: evidence is bound to an immutable candidate digest, not to 'now'.

decisions.decision: Rejected: excluding .agents/** from evidence key computation (or from the task-ledger roots) to dodge the self-reference.
decisions.rationale: task-ledger's check is make component-contracts, and that test suite validates .agents content itself (TestCanonicalTaskStateMigration, TestActiveEvidenceIndex, TestHistoricalBootstrapRecordsAndIndexes). If ledger content no longer entered the key, a ledger edit would keep stale 'passed' evidence for the very check that validates it, breaking validation.md section 8 freshness and reproducing the V2-024 stale-identity failure mode. It also breaks validation.md section 11 item 1-2 (every tracked file belongs to a component whose declared surface is verified). If the key scope were changed anyway, the tests put at risk are internal/ci TestCandidateComponentsDoesNotRequireUnchangedEvidence (key semantics) and, indirectly, every contracts test that would silently keep passing on stale evidence; no test currently pins 'the key covers .agents', so the regression would be invisible, which is a further reason to reject.

decisions.decision: The implementer does not write .agents/v2/task-state/** or .agents/v2/packets/**. Terra records the V2-008 transition after the work order validates.
decisions.rationale: internal/contracts TestCanonicalTaskStateMigration pins V2-008 to status queued with next_owner terra, so any status transition by the implementer fails make check and make candidate and would force an edit to internal/contracts/contracts_test.go, which is outside this work order and is an invariant/ledger decision owned by the coordinator.

decisions.decision: docs/architecture/validation.md section 11 gains a short subsection describing the aggregate attestation procedure (evidence-all, candidate, evidence-keys, identity injection, two-commit protocol and the one-component re-mint).
decisions.rationale: docs/policies/README.md requires one source of truth for a fact and Increment Done requires the evidence procedure to be resumable from the checkpoint alone; a new entrypoint and a non-obvious ordering rule are otherwise unrecoverable from code. docs/** is owned by the docs component whose check is a cheap ripgrep gate, so the added cost is negligible.

verification: devbox run --pure -- make check (timeout 1800s) is green at commit A and at commit B
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-all EVIDENCE_TASK_ID=V2-008 EVIDENCE_CORRELATION_ID=v2-008-candidate-gate (timeout 1800s) writes 23 records under build/evidence
devbox run --pure -- make candidate (timeout 300s) prints {"candidate":true} at commit A
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys (timeout 300s) prints evidence_keys for all 23 components
every generated build/evidence record has task_id V2-008 and correlation_id v2-008-candidate-gate; no record contains V2-005 or m0-candidate
devbox run --pure -- go run ./cmd/ci-plan --execute --all --task-id BAD exits non-zero without writing any record

devbox run --pure -- make affected BASE=5cf092e (timeout 1800s) still succeeds with no new flags, proving scripts/affected.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml compatibility, and its records carry task_id V2-000
devbox run --pure -- make component-ci (timeout 600s) passes including the new cmd/ci-plan identity test

after staging commit B, devbox run --pure -- make component COMPONENT=task-ledger EVIDENCE_TASK_ID=V2-008 EVIDENCE_CORRELATION_ID=v2-008-candidate-gate then devbox run --pure -- make candidate (timeout 600s each) is green
devbox run --pure -- make ownership (timeout 300s) shows the new .agents files have exactly one owner
python3 -c "import hashlib;print(hashlib.sha256(open('.agents/v2/evidence/V2-008-candidate-aggregate.json','rb').read()).hexdigest())" equals the index entry evidence_hash
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys | jq -r '.evidence_keys|to_entries|sort_by(.key)|.[]|"\(.key)\n\(.value)"' | sha256sum equals the attestation evidence_key when run at base_commit
risks: Cold caches: make evidence-all runs the whole graph (go test ./... , the Firestore emulator, gitleaks, tofu init). Warm-cache measurement in the coordinator worktree was 12s for 23 components and 0.1s for make candidate, but a cold run needs the 1800s timeout.

component-infra runs tofu init -backend=false, which fetches the lock-pinned provider from the OpenTofu registry. This is a pinned toolchain fetch with no credentials, but it fails offline; that is escalation E3, not a reason to skip infra evidence.

Evidence keys follow the git index plus working-tree content, so a dirty or partially staged tree silently shifts keys. All generation must run on a clean staged tree, otherwise make candidate reports a stale key mismatch.

build/evidence accumulates records for superseded keys; ci.CandidateComponents reads by exact filename so this is harmless, but a stale directory can mask a missing regeneration. rm -rf build/evidence before the final run.

The default V2-000 identity means CI runs (make affected) keep producing unattributed local evidence. That is intentional for this task; giving CI runs a real correlation identity is follow-up work, not part of V2-008.

The attestation is bound to base_commit; once the v2 branch advances past commit B the recorded keys are historical and re-attestation is required. This is validation.md section 8 freshness, not a defect.
